work_order.understanding: All three review findings from PR #60 still reproduce on main, and I confirmed each by running the suite rather than reading it alone. (1) ORDER IS UNASSERTED: `skipLinkFocusesMain` at test/web/pages.test.js:146-159 finds the skip link by scanning every `<a>` in the document for `href="#main"` and finds `<main>` by a bare `/<main\b([^>]*)>/`, with no comparison between the two offsets. I applied the reviewer's relocation to src/web/pages.js (moved the skip link from pages.js:68 to after `</main>`) and ran `node --test test/web/pages.test.js`: 51 pass / 0 fail, unchanged from baseline. The bypass the ticket exists for is destroyed and the suite is green. (2) NO FORCED-COLORS CARVE-OUT: src/web/styles.css:116-118 sets `outline: none` on `#main:focus` unconditionally. `grep -rn 'forced-colors' src/ test/` returns nothing, so no mode restores an indicator. (3) UNDECLARED MATCHER RELAXATION: test/web/pages.test.js:116 is `/<main\b[^>]*>([\s\S]*?)<\/main>/` — the `id="main"` requirement present before #52 is gone, so the heading-hierarchy assertion now holds for *some* `<main>` rather than the skip link's target. I verified the reviewer's proposed replacement `/<main\b[^>]*\bid="main"[^>]*>([\s\S]*?)<\/main>/` against all five shapes: it matches `<main id="main">`, `<main id="main" tabindex="-1">` and `<main tabindex="-1" id="main">` (and tolerates a fourth attribute), and rejects both `<main>` and `<main id="other">`, where the current regex accepts both. These are one ticket, not three: (1) and (3) are the same defect class in the same helper family nine lines apart, and (2) is the stylesheet half of the same skip-link bypass. I take the reviewer's primary fix in all three cases; on (2) I am restoring the indicator rather than documenting the omission, because in forced-colors Chromium honours `outline: none` and substitutes nothing while every other focusable element keeps its ring, leaving `<main>` the only focusable thing on the page with no indicator.
work_order.root_cause: The #52 guard checks each element's own attributes but never their relationship. `skipLinkFocusesMain` proves the link exists, the class is right, and main is focusable — but 'exists somewhere in the document' satisfies all three while the link sits below `</main>`. The same helper family then relaxed `mainOf` past the point the work order described, dropping the `id="main"` requirement along with the tag text, and the stylesheet rule that suppresses the focus ring was written without considering the mode that strips author colours.

review.detail:
The new forced-colors test does not assert the one property the work order names as its own failure mode — that the carve-out comes AFTER the bare #main:focus rule. The block is found anywhere in the file, so a stylesheet where the carve-out silently loses on source order still passes this test; it is caught only incidentally, by the older suppression test, with a misleading diagnostic.

`test/web/pages.test.js:256`

Evidence: Mutation E: moved the '@media (forced-colors: active) { #main:focus { outline: 2px solid CanvasText; } }' block to sit BEFORE the bare '#main:focus { outline: none; }' rule, where both selectors are 1,1,0 and the later one wins, so the carve-out does not apply. `node --test test/web/pages.test.js` -> 52 pass / 1 fail, and the single failure is 'the #main focus suppression still carries the declaration the skip target depends on' (test 7). The new test 'the #main focus suppression is restored inside forced-colors...' (test 8) PASSES. Its regex /@media\s*\(forced-colors:\s*active\)\s*\{[^@]*?#main:focus\s*\{([^}]*)\}/ at line 256 has no positional constraint, so it matches the block wherever it sits. The regression does surface, but the message a developer sees is 'the focused landmark paints no ring' — because the pre-existing test's /#main:focus\s*\{([^}]*)\}/ now first-matches the carve-out and sees 'outline: 2px solid CanvasText' — which points at the wrong declaration. work-order risks[2] names this exact ordering as the thing that must not regress.

Fix: Add an index comparison inside the forced-colors test: assert the carve-out's match index is greater than the bare rule's match index (e.g. exec both with /g and compare .index), so the test that owns forced-colors also owns its source order. Optional follow-on: the pre-existing test at line 242 should anchor on the bare rule (e.g. require the first #main:focus body to be exactly the suppression) so its diagnostic stops misfiring when the two rules swap.

qa.title: On every error shell the first Tab does not reach the skip link, because the Retry button autofocuses on load
qa.expected: On a fresh load with no prior interaction, the first element to receive focus is the skip link, on every route and in every state — including ?state=error, which AC-1's how_to_verify names explicitly.
qa.actual: Before any key is pressed, document.activeElement is already BUTTON[data-action="retry"] on all five error shells. The first Tab moves past the skip link: on /journal?state=error it lands on the first journal 'Open' button, and on /, /opportunities and /approvals it lands on <body> after focus has cycled out of the document. A keyboard or screen-reader user who lands on a failed page therefore never gets the skip link as their first stop, which is the exact moment they most need it. ?state=ideal/empty/loading/partial are unaffected.
repro: Serve the app: PORT=3000 npm run sdlc:serve
Open http://localhost:3000/journal?state=error in a fresh browser window
Press no key; in the console run document.activeElement — it is the Retry BUTTON, not <body>
Press Tab once; document.activeElement is BUTTON.button.journal-open, not the skip link
Control: open http://localhost:3000/journal (no ?state=) and repeat — the first Tab does land on A.skip-link
Reproduces identically on all five routes with ?state=error, and identically on origin/main (served on a second port) — it is pre-existing, not caused by PR #62
qa.suspected_cause: src/web/client.js:36-40 runs `var failedRetry = document.querySelector('.panel-error [data-action="retry"]'); if (failedRetry) { failedRetry.focus(); }` unconditionally on load, before the user has pressed anything. It sets the focus entry point deep in the document. The new ordering lock in test/web/pages.test.js:153-171 compares document *offsets* (skip.index < main.index) and cannot see a programmatic focus pre-emption, so no test in the suite covers the focus *order* the skip link exists to guarantee. The fix is a maintainer call: either drop the autofocus on load, or scope it so it does not pre-empt the first Tab, or amend AC-1 to exclude the error state — I am not proposing which, because the autofocus is a deliberate, documented decision (see .sdlc/memory/qa/selectors.md, 'focused automatically on error pages, so keyboard assertions start there') and the two behaviours genuinely conflict.

qa.title: \bid="main" matches data-id="main", so both guards accept a main landmark that has lost its id
qa.expected: The heading-hierarchy matcher and the skip-link guard require the landmark to carry the real id="main" — the skip link's target. A <main data-id="main"> with no id is not that target and should be rejected by both.
qa.actual: Both guards use \b, and '-' is a non-word character, so \bid="main" matches the tail of data-id="main". With <main id="main" tabindex="-1"> changed to <main data-id="main" tabindex="-1"> in src/web/pages.js, test/web/pages.test.js on HEAD is 53 pass / 0 fail, and the page in a real browser serves a skip link whose href="#main" resolves to nothing: activating it leaves focus on the <a> rather than moving it into the landmark.
repro: Copy the repo to a scratch directory (do not edit the repo under test)
In src/web/pages.js, change the layout's '<main id="main" tabindex="-1">' to '<main data-id="main" tabindex="-1">'
Serve the scratch tree and open /: document.getElementById('main') is null

qa.suspected_cause: \b asserts a word boundary, not whitespace, so any hyphenated attribute ending in id satisfies it. A one-line change — require whitespace before the attribute, e.g. /\sid="main"/ — closes it in both places: mainOf at test/web/pages.test.js:28 (new in this diff) and the mainAttrs clause at :161 (unchanged context from origin/main). The new pin at :268 rejects <main> and <main id="other"> but not the data-id shape, which is the one hole left in the family it is meant to close.
